title: Unary Scan Loop
statement: Let $E$ be a finite bit string of length at most $B$, and let $o$ return the bit of $E$ at each natural-number position, defaulting to false beyond its end. Suppose the suffix of $E$ beginning at position $p$ consists of exactly $k$ true bits followed by a false bit and a remaining suffix. For either value of the Boolean flag $ex$, the scan machine, on input $X(n,w)$ and starting in state $uA(ex)$ with registers $(p,c,0)$ and no result, can reach state $uE(ex)$ with registers $(p+k,c,k)$ and no result, with every register bounded by $B$ at all intermediate configurations.
hypotheses_covered: The oracle agrees with $E$ on every position, defaulting to false out of range
The suffix of $E$ at position $p$ is $k$ true bits followed by false and a remaining suffix
The run maintains the register bound $B$
